purpose: Replace FTA as the gating attack-effectiveness metric. Establish a multi-metric BETA-baseline that Phase 1 RL policy will be compared against.
test_protocol: BETA reimpl (saliency selector + eigenvector centrality prune + PGD with B=5, eps=0.1, alpha=0.01, 10 iters x 5 restarts) on 200 sampled detected (window, target=argmax) pairs. Per-sensor scores patched into test set; F1/PA-F1/AUC-PR recomputed over patched test set. Continuous target-score degradation reported per attack trial.
headline_metric: target_score_degradation (continuous, metric-agnostic, smooth signal for Phase 1 PPO reward)

interpretation.f1_reductions_small_by_design: Each attack patches only the score row of one (window, sensor) pair into the test set. With 200 / 17180 = 1.16% sampling rate, the global F1 metrics over the full test set move only fractionally. This is expected; it would require ~10000+ trials to make the F1 reduction statistically large. The continuous target_score_degradation metric does not have this dilution issue.
interpretation.target_score_degradation_mean_interpreta: GDN's mean degradation 18804 reflects the chronic sensor-106 mispredict (clean ~18950 → ~40 after attack on sensor 106 trials, with smaller deltas on the few non-106 trials). TopoGDN's mean 39135 reflects sensor 106's higher amplitude in TopoGDN (~38500 → ~40). Both detectors are 'attackable' via PGD on this victim — when the attacker can choose sensor 106 as target, score collapse is reliable.
interpretation.auc_pr_negative_for_topogdn: TopoGDN's AUC-PR went up by 0.00003 under attack — within noise. The attack's impact on global ranking is below the AUC-PR noise floor at this sample size.

phase1_reward_signal_validation.verdict: Continuous degradation provides usable Phase 1 RL signal with O(10^4) scale and O(10^3) per-trial std. Reward will need normalization for stability (z-score or min-max within episode), but signal-to-noise is non-trivial.

beta_target_topogdn_wadi.attack_FTA_at_B5: 0.6418 quoted from BETA Table for SWaT, not WADI

our_topogdn_wadi.attack_PA_F1_K10_oracle: not directly comparable; multi-metric uses unsmoothed residuals

comparison_to_beta_published.interpretation: BETA's published numbers cannot be directly side-by-side'd with our multi-metric numbers due to (a) Path A/A' baseline F1 gap already accepted, (b) multi-metric uses unsmoothed residuals while Path A used GDN's smoothed_err_scores 4-step rolling mean. The multi-metric framework is internally consistent: clean and attacked numbers use the same scoring pipeline, so attack EFFECT (reduction + degradation) is meaningful within our pipeline.

phase1_handoff.use_continuous_target_score_degradation: Phase 1 PPO reward should use clean_score(target) - attacked_score(target) directly. Sign convention: positive when attack succeeds. Magnitude varies per target: ~100 for non-pathological sensors, ~10000-40000 for sensor 106.
phase1_handoff.potential_signal_pathology_to_address_in: Sensor 106's chronic mispredict means easy reward gains by always attacking that sensor. Phase 1 may need to either (a) penalize repeatedly attacking the same sensor across windows, (b) restrict to non-106 targets during training, or (c) accept that the policy learns to exploit sensor 106 — which is itself a useful adversarial finding (BETA-style attacks easily succeed against this victim by targeting sensor 106).
phase1_handoff.supplementary_metrics: Track raw F1 / PA-F1 / AUC-PR reduction over a periodic full-test-set patched evaluation. Won't provide per-step reward but tracks aggregate progress.

limitations: 200 trials per (detector, seed) is sparse; F1 reduction below noise floor.
Unsmoothed residuals — diverges from Path A's GDN-evaluate-pipeline numbers (which use 4-step rolling mean) by ~20pp on absolute F1.
Single seed per detector. Phase 1 may want to evaluate against the full 9-10-seed ensemble for robustness.
Sensor 106 chronic mispredict dominates the degradation distribution; mean is biased high.
